rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Monday, July 20, 2026, Line 1, PETITIONER MIA SHEW-SMITH's Notice Of Hearing. It appears that the facts material to Mia Shew-Smith's arbitration demand are the same as the facts material to Michelle Harrison's petition. The court's indicated is to adopt the Harrison order in its entirety as to Shew-Smith. Shew-Smith shall prepare a proposed order using the Harrison order as a template (with the duplicated paragraph on page 5 omitted) and shall serve the proposed order on Sephora according to Rule of Court 3.1312 before providing it to the court. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA).

Matter on calendar for Monday, July 20, 2026, Line 3, PETITIONER ILENE STURROCK's Notice Of Hearing (On Petition). Sephora presents evidence that Ilene Sturrock signed up for the Beauty Insider program online in 2007. (Sephora Compendium, pdf p. 36.) Neither party has presented evidence of the terms of the Beauty Insider program at that time. Sturrock states in her declaration that she had an online account and used it within the 10 months prior to filing her petition, but there is no evidence that she was presented with or accepted any BITC prior to March 15, 2024, the date she signed her declaration. Sephora published the March 2024 BITC, which did not have an arbitration clause, the preceding day. (Id., pdf p. 65 [Gagin Decl., 2].) The court continues the petition for hearing to October 20, 2026 and grants Sephora's request to authorize mutual discovery concerning Sturrock's actual or constructive notice and acceptance of Beauty Insider terms containing an arbitration clause. Because a petition to compel arbitration is supposed to be a summary proceeding, the court is open to setting another informal discovery conference with the parties to discuss the scope of discovery during the brief discovery window to manage discovery efficiently. rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Monday, July 20, 2026, Line 37, ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE RE PRELIMINARY INJUNCTION. The order to show cause re preliminary injunction is discharged and the court denies the request for preliminary injunction. The temporary restraining order that was previously entered is dissolved. Plaintiff Natasha Blum has not filed a proof of service showing that any defendant has been served with the order to show cause. Rule of Court 3.1150, subdivision (a), requires that, "[i]f the responding party has not appeared, the OSC must be served in the same manner as a summons and complaint." Because the responding party has not appeared and there is no proof of service of the OSC in the same manner as a summons and complaint, the court may not issue a preliminary injunction.
